title: GazeGuard: Detecting Interview Anxiety via Multimodal Gaze and Audio Features
abstract: We present GazeGuard, a system for detecting signs of interview anxiety using an ensemble of gaze, audio, and video features. We evaluate our approach on a dataset of simulated interview sessions.
draft_text:
1. Introduction: Interview anxiety affects candidate performance significantly. Prior work has looked at facial expression analysis but not combined gaze steadiness with audio prosody in an ensemble anomaly detection framework.

2. Related Work: Several papers have studied affect detection in interviews using video alone.

3. Method: We extract gaze steadiness scores, audio pitch variance, and use an ensemble anomaly detection model to flag anxious moments. Features are combined and fed into the model.

4. Results: The system successfully flags anxious moments in our test recordings.

5. Conclusion: GazeGuard shows promise for interview coaching applications.
